nodes.text: Let $G$ be a graph with minimum degree $k$ and girth $>2s$ (i.e. $G$ contains no cycles of length $\leq 2s$). Must there be $\gg k^s$ many distinct cycle lengths in $G$?

#752 : [Er92b] [Er93,p.346] [Er94b] graph theory | cycles A question of Erdős, Faudree, and Schelp, who proved it when $s=2$. The answer is yes, proved by Sudakov and Verstraëte [SuVe08] , who in fact proved that under the assumption of average degree $k$ and girth $>2s$ there are at least $\gg k^s$ many consecutive even integers which are cycle lengths in $G$.
